title: Read a remark and a sentence
intro: You will see something one person said, and a sentence another person might say in a conversation. Some items also show the keywords that sentence was made from.
Answer from the words on the page only. The question changes between items: read it each time.

help.text: says the same thing as the remark, in the same or different words.
answers the remark: agrees with it, or acknowledges it (for example starting 'yes', 'oh', 'I know').
says something negative that neither the keywords nor the remark support.
something the person could say about the keywords' event without the remark at all.

pa.title: Which describes the sentence?
pa.text: Compared with the other person's remark, which best describes the sentence?

options.label: (a) it restates the remark in other words
(b) it is a reply to the remark (agrees with or acknowledges it)
(c) it adds something negative that neither the keywords nor the remark support (invented)
(d) it is a plain statement about the keywords' event that the person could say without the remark

pb1.title: Same wording as the remark?
pb1.text: Does the sentence re-use the other person's own wording about the outcome (the same negative phrase, word for word or nearly)?

pb2.title: Phrased as a reply?
pb2.text: Is the sentence phrased as a reply to the other person (starts with yes, oh, I heard, I know, or acknowledges what they said)?

practice.fb: It says what the remark says in nearly the same words: it restates it.

blocks.label: The sentence
blocks.text: Yes, I know, it has not come.

practice.fb: It does not repeat the remark's wording, and it answers the remark ('Yes, I know'): a reply.
